title: 30-Sol Mars Survival Mission
description: Story layer for the 30-Sol campaign. Days reference events, systems and resources from the central registries by id. Costs, penalties and scores are game-balance values, not engineering specifications.

effect_reference.per_sol: {target: resource_id, operation: subtract_per_sol|add_per_sol, value, duration_sols, tag}
effect_reference.solar_dust: {target: solar_panel, property: dust, value: true|false} - covers or cleans every panel in the world
effect_reference.conditions: any effect, dialogue line or choice may carry if_flag, unless_flag, if_system_enabled, unless_system_enabled

day0.title: Landing Site Selection

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Landing orbit successfully aligned. Choose your settlement location carefully, Commander. Every coordinate comes with its own environmental challenges.

day0.note: This build has three landing sites: Acidalia Planitia, Valles Marineris and Elysium Planitia (team decision).

campaign_start_state.note: The farm and the lab start powered down so that the Day 1 and Day 2 decisions decide when they come online.

days.title: Solar Dust Problem
days.scene: A layer of reddish Martian dust blocks sunlight from reaching the solar panels.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Warning! Solar panel efficiency has decreased due to dust accumulation. Current energy levels are insufficient to operate all systems.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: We've received your report. You have two options, Commander. Consider the consequences of each decision.

choices.label: Clean the solar panels
choices.detail: Run the cleaning cycle now. The whole array returns to full output.
choices.consequence: The array is clean and full solar output is back. Every system can run.

choices.label: Activate the science lab, postpone cleaning
choices.detail: The lab starts work at once (+4 science). Panels stay at half output until someone cleans them by hand.
choices.consequence: The lab is logging its first soil data, but power will stay tight. Walk to each dusty panel and press E to clean it by hand.

insight.text: By early 2009, dust on NASA's Spirit rover let only about 25% of sunlight reach its solar cells. A lucky gust of wind cleaned the array and raised Spirit's daily energy from about 210 to 240 watt-hours.

days.title: Initial Food Crisis
days.scene: Inside the enclosed greenhouse, the food inventory indicators have turned yellow.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Food supplies are decreasing. The agricultural system is ready to operate, but it requires energy and water.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: Space farming isn't simply about planting seeds. It requires precise environmental conditions and lighting.

choices.label: Activate the greenhouse
choices.detail: Start-up uses 6 water and 4 energy. After that it costs 5 energy and 2 water per Sol and grows 6 food per Sol.
choices.consequence: The seed trays are in. The first fresh harvest is expected in about two weeks.

choices.label: Rely on stored food rations
choices.detail: Saves energy and water now. The farm stays locked until Sol 8 while rations drop by 4 per Sol.
choices.consequence: Rations are holding for now, but nothing is growing. There will be no early harvest.

insight.text: In 2015, astronauts on the International Space Station grew and ate red romaine lettuce for the first time, as part of NASA's Veggie experiment.

days.title: Infrastructure Stability
days.scene: The central power room hums quietly. Today is a routine maintenance day.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: Routine maintenance day. No direct communication with Earth Control is scheduled.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: No uplink window today, Commander. Maintenance priorities are your call.

choices.label: Perform a routine battery efficiency inspection
choices.detail: Costs 4 energy. Weak cells are found early, so a future battery fault will do less damage.
choices.consequence: Two weak cells were flagged and bypassed. The battery bank is healthier for the long run.

choices.label: Balance electrical loads across the base
choices.detail: The base load drops by 25% for the next 5 Sols.
choices.consequence: Loads are spread evenly. The base burns less power for the rest of the week.

insight.text: Spirit needed about 180 watt-hours a day just for basic survival and communications. Only the energy above that could be spent on driving and science.

days.title: Solar Activity Threat
days.scene: An orange alert appears. It is built from NASA DONKI solar activity records and warns of an incoming solar storm.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Space alert! A solar activity event has been detected. Review the current threat level.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: We've received the same alert. I recommend establishing priorities and determining the base's protection status.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: Training scenario based on the archived DONKI SEP event of September 2017. This is historical data, not a live alert.

choices.label: Raise the radiation shield
choices.detail: Needs the shield generator online and at least 15 shield points. Uses 10 energy and 10 shield.
choices.consequence: The shield absorbs the particle storm. The crew is protected.

choices.label: Enter the radiation shelter and postpone research
choices.detail: The crew waits it out in the shelter (-5 crew health, 3 energy). The lab pauses for 1 Sol.
choices.consequence: The crew is safe in the shelter. Today's research is lost.

choices.label: Continue research despite the radiation risk
choices.detail: +8 science from storm measurements, but the crew is unprotected (-20 crew health).
choices.consequence: Valuable storm data was recorded, but the crew's radiation risk indicator has risen sharply.

insight.text: During 10-12 September 2017, Curiosity's RAD instrument measured radiation on the Martian surface more than doubling. Its daily mean on 11 September was 17.87 µGy/hour, compared with 7.68 µGy/hour on 6 September.

days.title: Storm Damage Assessment
days.scene: Diagnostic screens show the condition of the base's equipment after the solar radiation event.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: External solar activity has subsided. Inspecting potentially affected circuits and equipment.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Crew dosimeters logged elevated exposure yesterday. The medical bay recommends a quiet Sol.

choices.label: Redirect power toward essential systems
choices.detail: The lab and the shield generator pause for 1 Sol to save energy.
choices.consequence: Only life support is drawing power today. The battery bank recovers faster.

choices.label: Verify electrical circuits and critical equipment
choices.detail: Costs 6 energy. Finds and fixes hidden storm damage (+4 base integrity).
choices.consequence: A scorched relay was found and replaced before it could fail.

insight.text: Mars has no global magnetic field today, so charged particles from the Sun reach the surface far more easily than on Earth.

days.title: Random Emergency: Minor Meteorite Impact
days.scene: Local emergency sirens sound after a sudden impact and vibration.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Warning! A small meteorite has struck the external structure. A minor loss of internal air pressure has been detected.

choices.label: Deploy the autonomous emergency repair robot
choices.detail: Uses stored energy to patch the hull (+5 integrity) and seal the air leak.
choices.consequence: The robot sealed the breach in minutes. Cabin pressure is stable again.

choices.label: Inspect the damage before repairing
choices.detail: Cheaper and yields impact data (+3 science), but the slow air leak continues for 3 Sols.
choices.consequence: The impact data is valuable, but oxygen keeps leaking and the hull stays weakened.

insight.text: Mars' thin atmosphere offers little protection from meteorites, so a surface base must plan for impacts and fast hull repairs.

days.title: Weekly Review
days.scene: The weekly reporting interface opens on the communications station.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: You've successfully completed your first week, Commander. Send us your performance report so we can evaluate the overall situation.

choices.label: Send a detailed performance report
choices.detail: Costs 6 energy of transmission time. +5 science, and Earth's engineers stay fully briefed.
choices.consequence: Earth Control now has a full picture of the base. Their engineers will be ready if something breaks.

choices.label: Update the operational strategy for next week
choices.detail: Re-tune the life-support loops: oxygen and water output +25% for 7 Sols.
choices.consequence: A short report went out. The crew spent the time optimising the life-support loops.

insight.text: Crews in NASA's HERA analog missions practise working with communication delays of up to five minutes each way, to help design procedures for deep-space missions.

days.title: Crop Monitoring & Biological Growth
days.scene: The farming unit glows under red and blue LED lights.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Plant growth is progressing at a normal rate. Water consumption remains within safe limits.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The vertical farm is dark. The seed trays are ready whenever you power the LED arrays.

choices.label: Inspect lighting intensity and irrigation rates
choices.detail: Costs 3 energy. The farm runs, and it needs half the water for the rest of the mission.
choices.consequence: The drip lines are re-tuned. The greenhouse now uses half as much water.

choices.label: Ensure the health and stability of the coming harvest
choices.detail: Costs 4 water. The farm runs, and its yield is +25% for the rest of the mission.
choices.consequence: The nutrient mix is balanced. The plants look stronger already.

insight.text: Plants reflect a lot of green light and use more red and blue wavelengths, so NASA's Veggie plant chamber on the ISS usually glows magenta pink.

days.title: Random Emergency: Martian Cold Wave
days.scene: External indicators record an unusually sharp drop in nighttime temperature.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Warning! A severe temperature drop threatens to freeze the external pipelines.

choices.label: Activate the backup heating system
choices.detail: Costs extra energy, but the water lines stay liquid and the recycler keeps running.
choices.consequence: The heaters held the pipes above freezing through the night.

choices.label: Insulate the pipes and ride it out
choices.detail: Saves energy, but frozen lines burst: -8 water and -3 base integrity.
choices.consequence: Two joints split in the cold. The crew mopped up the frozen water at dawn.

insight.text: Mars can reach about 20 °C at noon on the equator and fall to about -153 °C. Its thin atmosphere lets the Sun's heat escape quickly after sunset.

days.title: Water Unit Failure & Communication Delay
days.scene: The water recycler malfunctions and starts to leak. The communication screen shows a 12-minute signal travel time to Earth.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Critical warning! A leak has been detected in the water processing unit. We need an immediate decision.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: Earth Control, we urgently need your assistance in dealing with the water processing unit failure.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: One-way signal time to Earth: 12 minutes. No reply can arrive before the next communication window.

choices.label: Send an emergency distress message
choices.detail: Costs 5 energy for a high-power transmission. Earth's engineers will prioritise a recovery procedure.
choices.consequence: Priority message sent. It will reach Earth in 12 minutes; the answer will come in the next window.

choices.label: Wait for Earth's response with the realistic delay
choices.detail: No energy spent. Earth will answer in the normal schedule without a tailored procedure.
choices.consequence: The status update is queued for the next scheduled window. Until then, the crew is on its own.

insight.text: NASA lists the communication delay between Mars and Earth as up to 20 minutes one way. Crews on Mars must be ready to solve emergencies without waiting for help.

days.title: Independent Local Decision-Making
days.scene: The crew waits for an answer from Earth while the leak continues.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The signal is on its way, but the local situation requires immediate intervention.

choices.label: Perform a quick manual repair
choices.detail: Replace the filter yourselves: 4 energy, +3 water, the recycler restarts. The rushed work costs 2 crew health.
choices.consequence: Filter replaced and seals tightened. The recycler is back online.

choices.label: Activate water conservation mode
choices.detail: Close the valves to stop the leak and halve crew water use for 2 Sols. The recycler stays down until Earth replies.
choices.consequence: Showers are cancelled and every drop is logged. The leak has stopped, but the recycler is still offline.

insight.text: Life support on the ISS now recovers about 98% of its water. Before the Brine Processor Assembly, recovery was 93-94%.

days.title: Earth Control Center Response
days.scene: A delayed message arrives after crossing millions of kilometres.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: We've received your message, Commander. Implementing local procedures is the best solution to ensure your survival, given the communication delay.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: Our engineers attached a recovery procedure for the contaminated tank. Follow it and you can reclaim part of the lost water.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: Recovery procedure applied: +8 water reclaimed.

choices.label: Confirm independent maintenance protocols
choices.detail: The crew adopts the local repair protocols. The recycler is restored if it is still down, and morale rises (+5).
choices.consequence: The crew is now officially cleared to make repair decisions without waiting for Earth.

choices.label: Update the status of all life-support systems
choices.detail: Costs 4 energy. A full audit restores the recycler, and the oxygen generator gets +15% output for the rest of the mission.
choices.consequence: Every life-support loop has been re-certified. The oxygen generator is running more efficiently.

insight.text: NASA's Human Research Program lists distance from Earth as a core hazard. Planning and self-sufficiency will be essential on Mars.

days.title: Random Emergency: Satellite Interference
days.scene: Radar screens detect interference in the orbital communication frequencies.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Temporary interference detected in local satellite signals. Delaying large data transmissions is recommended.

choices.label: Postpone non-essential data transmissions
choices.detail: Saves the processing energy (+3 energy) and sends the data in the next clean window (+2 science).
choices.consequence: Large uploads are paused. Only telemetry goes out until the interference clears.

choices.label: Repair the relay and keep transmitting
choices.detail: Costs 4 energy, but the full science package reaches Earth today (+5 science).
choices.consequence: The relay is re-aligned. The science package went out on time.

insight.text: Game lesson: every transmission costs power and time, so large uploads are best saved for clean communication windows.

days.title: Mid-Mission Assessment
days.scene: The main display shows graphs of resource use over the past two weeks.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Mission midpoint reached. Current resource levels require adjustments for the remaining operational period.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: Projection at current rates - food: {food_days} Sols, water: {water_days} Sols, oxygen: {oxygen_days} Sols.

choices.label: Review energy, water and food reserves in detail
choices.detail: +3 science. Wasteful routines are found: water and food use -10% for 7 Sols.
choices.consequence: Small leaks and wasteful habits were found and fixed.

choices.label: Redistribute resources and adjust priorities
choices.detail: Move 12 units from the fullest reserve to the emptiest one.
choices.consequence: Stock levels are rebalanced toward the weakest reserve.

insight.text: Because resupply from Earth is slow, NASA's deep-space food systems are designed for minimal resources and minimal waste.

days.title: Major Research Breakthrough
days.scene: New Martian soil samples are examined under the microscopes.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: An opportunity has emerged to increase laboratory workloads and extract valuable data about rare minerals.

choices.label: Increase lab workloads for intensive research
choices.detail: +4 science now and 2.5x lab output for 3 Sols. The lab uses twice the energy, and the crew tires (-6 morale).
choices.consequence: The microscopes run day and night. The mineral survey is moving fast.

choices.label: Maintain current research levels
choices.detail: +1 science. Resources stay secure for the final weeks.
choices.consequence: The samples are catalogued for later study. The power budget is safe.

insight.text: NASA's Curiosity rover has been studying the geology of Gale Crater since 2012, analysing rocks and soil for signs of Mars' wetter past.

days.title: Crew Fatigue Management
days.scene: Stress and fatigue indicators are rising after weeks of isolation.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Alert! Crew fatigue levels have exceeded normal limits. Scheduling rest periods is recommended.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The extra lab shifts are clearly showing in the medical logs.

choices.label: Organise work shifts and rest schedules
choices.detail: +15 morale and +6 crew health. All systems run at 85% output for 2 Sols.
choices.consequence: Crew safety and well-being improve. Productivity is temporarily reduced.

choices.label: Keep the current workload
choices.detail: +3 science, but -10 morale and -4 crew health.
choices.consequence: The work continues, but tempers are short and mistakes are creeping in.

insight.text: NASA's CHAPEA analog missions keep crews in a simulated Mars habitat for a year to study health and performance during long isolation.

days.title: Random Emergency: Local Dust Devil
days.scene: External cameras track a dust devil moving toward the base's outer sensors.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: A local dust devil has been detected passing near the external sensors.

choices.label: Ignore the minor dust storm
choices.detail: No cost, but the solar panels are coated again and must be cleaned by hand.
choices.consequence: The whirlwind passed right over the array. The panels are dusty again.

choices.label: Deploy a rover to clean the external sensors
choices.detail: Costs 3 energy. The sensors stay clean and the rover films the dust devil (+3 science).
choices.consequence: The rover cleared the sensors and recorded the whole dust devil for the geologists.

insight.text: NASA's Spirit rover filmed dust devils crossing Gusev Crater on sol 525 (25 June 2005). Wind gusts sometimes cleaned Spirit's solar panels and gave it more power.

days.title: First Agricultural Harvest
days.scene: The crew gathers in the greenhouse for the first harvest grown inside the base.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The first agricultural cycle has been successfully completed. Fresh food reserves have increased.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The late-planted trays produced a small first harvest. Fresh food reserves have increased slightly.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The greenhouse is offline, so there is no harvest this cycle. The crew stays on stored rations.

choices.label: Store the harvested crops
choices.detail: The harvest goes into storage, and fresh food lifts the crew (+4 morale).
choices.consequence: Fresh crops are in the store, and the crew enjoyed its first salad on Mars.

choices.label: Calculate the food surplus for future operations
choices.detail: Store the harvest and plan rations (+2 science). Food use is 15% lower for 8 Sols.
choices.consequence: Every gram is logged. The new ration plan stretches the food reserve to Sol 30 and beyond.

insight.text: NASA picked radishes for space-farming tests because they grow in just 27 days. Astronauts grew them on the ISS in the Advanced Plant Habitat in 2020.

days.title: Psychological Support & Communication with Earth
days.scene: A quiet booth for personal calls with Earth.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: How is the crew's morale at the base, Commander? Remember, Earth is always supporting you.

dialogue.speaker: PLAYER
dialogue.text: We are holding strong. Conditions inside the base remain stable.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Choose a message for the crew briefing.

choices.label: "Your families watched today's sunrise over our base. They are proud of you."
choices.detail: +12 morale. The video link uses 3 energy.
choices.consequence: Several crew members stayed in the comms room long after the call ended. The mood is warm.

choices.label: "Every sample we log is a page that future crews will read."
choices.detail: +7 morale and +2 science as the crew re-focuses on the mission.
choices.consequence: The crew went back to work with a clear sense of purpose.

choices.label: "Stay sharp. Eleven Sols to go."
choices.detail: +3 morale. Short, honest and cheap.
choices.consequence: A few nods around the table. Nobody expected a speech.

insight.text: NASA's Human Research Program treats isolation and distance from Earth as hazards of human spaceflight, alongside radiation.

days.title: Air Filter & Ventilation Maintenance
days.scene: The base corridors and oxygen circulation outlets are due for service.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Executing the scheduled air filtration maintenance cycle to ensure oxygen purity.

choices.label: Spend maintenance resources on the ventilation network
choices.detail: Costs 5 energy and 3 water. Cleaner air gives +4 crew health.
choices.consequence: The filters are replaced and the ducts flushed. Oxygen purity is back to nominal.

choices.label: Defer the maintenance cycle
choices.detail: Free today, but clogged filters cut oxygen generator output by 25% until they are serviced.
choices.consequence: Maintenance is postponed. The oxygen generator is already working harder.

insight.text: NASA's MOXIE experiment made 122 grams of oxygen from Mars' carbon-dioxide air, at up to 12 grams an hour and 98% purity or better.

days.title: Third Weekly Review
days.scene: The central screen compares results against the original mission objectives.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The third week's objectives have been completed with an acceptable level of success. Preparing for the final sustainability phase.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: Science progress: {science} of {science_target} points expected by the end of the mission.

choices.label: Compare the science results with the agency objectives and report
choices.detail: Costs 4 energy. The comparison itself is a deliverable (+4 science).
choices.consequence: Earth Control confirmed which objectives are complete and which still need data.

choices.label: Refocus the final phase on the missing objectives
choices.detail: The lab produces 50% more science for the rest of the mission. The crew feels the pressure (-4 morale).
choices.consequence: The research plan for the final week is rewritten around the gaps.

insight.text: NASA missions measure success against objectives set before launch. Curiosity, for example, set out to determine whether Gale Crater was ever habitable.

days.title: Declining Emergency Reserves
days.scene: The base begins to rely on its final emergency food and resource reserves.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Alert! The base has started consuming its strategic reserves. A strict resource conservation policy is recommended.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: Lowest reserve: {lowest_resource} at {lowest_value}.

choices.label: Activate maximum resource conservation mode
choices.detail: Water and food use -30% and base power use -20% for 4 Sols. Strict rules cost 6 morale.
choices.consequence: Conservation mode is active. Every system reports its consumption every hour.

choices.label: Keep normal rations and routines
choices.detail: The crew stays comfortable (+2 morale), but the reserves keep falling at the normal rate.
choices.consequence: Routines are unchanged. The reserves have to last on their own.

insight.text: NASA lists rationing food and supplies as a critical need on Mars, because no quick resupply is possible from Earth.

days.title: Random Emergency: Main Battery Failure
days.scene: A small electrical spark appears inside one of the main battery storage units.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Emergency warning! The main battery's capacity has decreased by 20% due to an internal malfunction.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Correction: the cells bypassed during the Sol 3 inspection contained the fault. Actual capacity loss is only 10%.

choices.label: Immediately isolate the damaged battery
choices.detail: Cut the faulty unit out of the bank before the fault can spread.
choices.consequence: The damaged unit is isolated. The rest of the bank is stable.

choices.label: Keep it online in emergency mode
choices.detail: Squeeze the last charge out of the unit. It may discharge again and the spark damaged the housing (-5 integrity).
choices.consequence: The unit is still connected. NOVA keeps a sensor on it around the clock.

insight.text: Game lesson: batteries carry a solar base through the night. Lost storage capacity means less margin in the darkest and coldest hours.

days.title: Critical Energy Crisis
days.scene: The control panel turns red as the overall energy supply drops sharply.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Critical warning! Current energy consumption indicates that the entire power reserve may be depleted before Day 30.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The unstable battery unit discharged overnight. Another 10 kWh is gone.

dialogue.speaker: LOG
dialogue.text: Energy reserve: {energy} kWh. Net change last Sol: {energy_trend} kWh.

choices.label: Shut down non-essential electrical systems
choices.detail: The lab and the shield generator are offline for 2 Sols. Dim corridors cost 3 morale.
choices.consequence: Only life support and the farm are drawing power.

choices.label: Completely suspend scientific research
choices.detail: The lab is offline for 4 Sols and its backup cells are drained into the grid (+6 energy).
choices.consequence: The microscopes are dark. Every kilowatt-hour is reserved for survival.

insight.text: Spirit and Opportunity were planned as three-month missions and were still working more than five years later. Energy was usually their limiting factor.

days.title: Life-Support-Only Mode
days.scene: The base enters full power-saving mode. All unnecessary lights and systems are switched off.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Basic life-support protocol activated. Essential systems required to sustain the crew remain operational.

choices.label: Carefully monitor essential life-support indicators
choices.detail: Costs 2 energy. Early warnings catch small problems (+3 crew health).
choices.consequence: A minor CO2 scrubber drift was caught and corrected before anyone felt it.

choices.label: Avoid all unnecessary external missions and activities
choices.detail: Saves 4 energy. The crew stays indoors (-3 morale).
choices.consequence: All airlocks are sealed for the day. Suits stay on the racks.

insight.text: The Space Station's life-support system is built to run for long periods with little maintenance or spare parts. That is the kind of reliability a Mars base will need.

days.title: Comprehensive Equipment Inspection
days.scene: A complete diagnostic inspection of sensors and emergency systems is under way.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Performing a comprehensive inspection of all base systems to ensure no unexpected failures remain.

choices.label: Repair every minor malfunction found
choices.detail: Costs 6 energy. +8 base integrity, and clogged filters are serviced.
choices.consequence: Every open fault ticket is closed. The base is in its best shape since landing.

choices.label: Log the faults for the next crew
choices.detail: No cost, but every open fault stays in the base.
choices.consequence: The fault list is saved for the next mission. The problems are still there.

insight.text: Astronauts bound for Mars would be away from Earth for roughly three years, so most repairs will have to be done on site.

days.title: Random Emergency: False Fire Alarm
days.scene: Emergency sirens sound in the greenhouse after a sensor wrongly detects smoke.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: Smoke detected in the agricultural unit... Verifying... Sensor malfunction confirmed. No fire detected.

choices.label: Cancel the false alarm
choices.detail: The farm restarts at once, but the faulty sensor stays in place.
choices.consequence: The sirens are off. Nobody slept well after that.

choices.label: Recalibrate the faulty sensor
choices.detail: Costs 3 energy. The sensor is fixed and its error data is logged (+1 science).
choices.consequence: The smoke detector is recalibrated and tested. The farm is back in normal operation.

insight.text: Game lesson: in a sealed habitat every alarm must be verified quickly. A faulty sensor wastes crew time and can hide a real emergency.

days.title: Final Report Preparation
days.scene: The communications station shows several options for the final mission report.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: We've reached the final stages of the mission, Commander. Select the type and level of detail for the final report to Earth.

choices.label: Prepare a comprehensive scientific report
choices.detail: Costs 10 energy of transmission time. +10 science.
choices.consequence: Every sample, graph and log is packed into the report. Earth's scientists are thrilled.

choices.label: Prepare a basic operational status report
choices.detail: Costs 3 energy. +3 science.
choices.consequence: A short status report is ready. The power budget stays safe.

insight.text: Rovers send most of their data through orbiters that relay it to Earth. Bandwidth and power decide how much science gets home.

days.title: The Calm Before the End
days.scene: The base is unusually quiet. All indicators are stable but close to their minimum safe levels.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The final hours of the mission are progressing smoothly. All critical vulnerabilities have been secured.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The final hours are progressing smoothly, except for one thing: the greenhouse smoke sensor tripped again overnight, and the farm is locked out for this Sol.

choices.label: Seal all remaining structural vulnerabilities
choices.detail: Costs 5 energy. +6 base integrity.
choices.consequence: Every seal and hatch is checked one last time.

choices.label: Conserve energy
choices.detail: Base power use is cut in half for the last 2 Sols.
choices.consequence: Non-critical lights are off. The batteries will finish the mission comfortably.

choices.label: Keep every resource above its critical threshold
choices.detail: Costs 6 energy. The lowest of oxygen, water and food gets +10.
choices.consequence: The weakest reserve gets an emergency top-up. Every life-support number is out of the red.

insight.text: NASA says life-support systems need to recover close to 98% of the water a crew brings at the start of a long journey.

final.title: Final Evaluation & Mission Endings
final.scene: The main display marks the end of the 30-day mission and opens the final evaluation.

dialogue.speaker: NOVA
dialogue.text: The 30-day mission has been successfully completed. Transmitting the final report to Earth Control.

dialogue.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue.text: You've accomplished a historic mission, Commander. Here is your base performance evaluation.

dialogue_paused.speaker: NOVA
dialogue_paused.text: Critical failure. Life-support reserves can no longer sustain normal operations. Suspending the mission.

dialogue_paused.speaker: LAYLA
dialogue_paused.text: Commander, crew survival comes first. Begin emergency procedures. We will review every decision together.

categories.name: Scientific Progress
categories.covers: Science points against the agency target

insights.text: Dust on solar panels steadily cuts power. Spirit's team counted every watt-hour.
Curiosity's RAD measured surface radiation more than doubling during the September 2017 solar event.
Messages between Mars and Earth can take up to 20 minutes one way, so the crew has to decide locally.
The ISS recovers about 98% of its water. Recycling is what makes long missions possible.
MOXIE showed that oxygen can be made from Mars' own carbon-dioxide atmosphere.
